pointsOfInterest.description: This historic house stands on a tract of land in Pelham Bay Park that was purchased from the Siwanoy Indians in 1654 by Thomas Pell, an English doctor of medicine who had settled in Connecticut. pointsOfInterest.name: E.M.T. Christopher J. Prescott Playground — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: What was here before? Staten Island’s South Shore was formed by clay, sand, and gravel deposited by the Wisconsin glacier. pointsOfInterest.name: Captain Roald Amundsen Plaza — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: Roald Engelbregt Gravning Amundsen (1872-1928), polar explorer, was born in Borge, Norway. pointsOfInterest.name: Leonard Triangle — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: What was here before? This was once the property of Sir Roderick Cameron (1825-1900), a businessman who co-founded the R.W. Cameron and Company shipping line. pointsOfInterest.name: Graniteville Park — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: Graniteville Park, acquired by Parks in 1971, is located in northwestern Staten Island, at Jules Drive, Elson Court, and Regis Drive. pointsOfInterest.description: What was here before? The land encompassing this park and the General Charles W. Berry Houses was once occupied by the Richmond County Fair Grounds. pointsOfInterest.name: Gerard P. Dugan Playground — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: What was here before? Originally home to the Lenape, this property was owned by farmer John B. Cole, Sr. by the early 1800s. pointsOfInterest.description: The unique topography of Mariner's Marsh Park has arisen partly from human handiwork, with nature completing the setting. pointsOfInterest.name: William E. Kelly Park — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: What was here before? In 1890, this site was part of the J.R. Stillwell estate. pointsOfInterest.name: Alice Austen House and Park — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: What was here before? Before the arrival of Europeans and enslaved people, the Lenape lived on the land that would eventually be called Staten Island. pointsOfInterest.name: Wolfe’s Pond Park — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: The landscape of Wolfe’s Pond Park on Raritan Bay is rich in history, both natural and manmade. The beach was formed nearly 20,000 years ago during the last part of the ice age. pointsOfInterest.name: Roberto Clemente Ballfield — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: The Roberto Clemente Ballfield is named for one of this country’s greatest major league baseball players. pointsOfInterest.description: Commander Eugene S. Sarsfield (1902-43) served his country with distinction during World War II and went down with his ship, the U.S.S. pointsOfInterest.description: "There may be finer views than this in the world, but I don't believe it," said President Abraham Lincoln in 1864, when he exited his carriage on the crest that gives Brooklyn Heights its name. pointsOfInterest.name: Patrick O’Rourke Park — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: This playground is named for Patrick O’Rourke (1970-2001), a local citizen whose mistreatment during a medical procedure led to universal mandatory medical monitoring improvements. pointsOfInterest.name: The Old Stone House — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: The Old Stone House, also known as the Vechte-Courtelyou House, is a replica of a Dutch stone farmhouse that had a rich history. pointsOfInterest.name: Grace Playground — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: What was here before? This site was formerly occupied by several frame dwellings, which were razed to construct this playground. How did this site become a playground? pointsOfInterest.name: Rocco Torre Ballfields — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: These ballfields were dedicated in memory of Rocco Torre (1927-1996), veteran police officer and baseball lover, by Mayor Giuliani on August 15, 1997. pointsOfInterest.name: Salgado Playground — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: The former Patchen Playground was renamed for Police Officer Reinaldo Salgado (1956-1997) of the 81st Precinct in August 1997. pointsOfInterest.name: Hendrick I. Lott House — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: The Hendrick I. Lott House is one of fourteen remaining Dutch Colonial farmhouses in Kings County. It is listed on the National Register of Historic Places and is designated as a New York City Landmark. pointsOfInterest.name: McKinley Park — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: This park is named for William McKinley (1843-1901), twenty-fifth President of the United States. McKinley was born on January 29, 1843 in Niles, Ohio and attended Allegheny College in Meadville, Pennsylvania. pointsOfInterest.name: Canarsie Park — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: What was here before? The Canarsie resided here for thousands of years and called the area now known as the Flatlands, Keskateuw. pointsOfInterest.description: What was here before? The Canarsie lived in and around present-day Owl’s Head Park, fishing in the Hudson River and New York Harbor, collecting oysters on the shore, and farming the fertile outwash plain. pointsOfInterest.description: What was here before? This site was once part of Tunis Johnson’s (1838-1912) estate. pointsOfInterest.description: What was here before? pointsOfInterest.description: Ronald R. Edmonds (1935-1983) was an African American educational expert known for his commitment to improving public schools. pointsOfInterest.description: This ballfield was named in honor of firefighter and lifeguard Louis Valentino Jr. (1958-1996) under a local law introduced by Councilmember Stephen DiBrienza and signed by Mayor Giuliani on June 25, 1996. pointsOfInterest.description: Manhattan Beach was created by real estate developer Austin Corbin (1827-1896) in 1877 as a self-contained summer resort on 500 acres of salt marsh, the eastern peninsula of what was once Coney Island. pointsOfInterest.name: Cobble Hill Park — Historical Sign

pointsOfInterest.description: Commodore Barry Park is located in the Fort Greene neighborhood of Brooklyn. pointsOfInterest.name: Tilden Playground — Historical Sign

pointsOfInterest.name: Fort Greene Park — Historical Sign
pointsOfInterest.description: Fort Greene Park is a landmark, cherished for its history, rolling landscape, trees, and monuments. pointsOfInterest.description: Marshal Power (1922-1957) was a resident of Brooklyn who had a distinguished career in military and government service. pointsOfInterest.description: Named by naturalists Ron and Jean Bourque, Four Sparrow Marsh Preserve is home to four native species which require undisturbed marshland for nesting: Sharptailed, Seaside, Swamp, and Song Sparrows.
